evidence.quote:
SECTION 1: Council for the Village of South Bloomfield hereby imposes a new 180-day
moratorium on the receipt, processing, issuance, and approval of any application
for a zoning certificate and/or permit for any use related to data processing, hosting,
and related services (Data Centers).

SECTION 2: Council for the Village of South Bloomfield may rescind this moratorium at any
time prior to the expiration of 180 days. If necessary, it also may extend this
moratorium.
evidence.supports: New 180-day operative pause with early rescission/extension authority; signed May 18 passage date read visually on page 2, not OCR May 8.

decisions.notes: Correct the demonstrably false statement that no subsequent moratorium was found. The 2026 act uses both extending and new language; its relationship to the original, later actions, and current status remain unresolved. Baseline enacted_status is not confirmed.

current_status.from: Confirmed as of 2026-09-23: the 180-day moratorium (Ordinance 2025-28) expired on its own terms around 2026-06-13. Independent reporting from The Ohio Newsroom/Statehouse News Bureau (2026-02-26) and Scioto Post (2026-03) both describe South Bloomfield as having 'preemptively eliminat[ed] all areas of industrial zoning, in order to avoid applications from data centers,' corroborating the row's existing 'outcome' (new 2025 zoning book that does not list data centers as a permitted use). No extension or replacement moratorium was found; the village's approach has moved from a temporary pause to eliminating the zoning category itself.
current_status.to: Signed Ordinance 2026-06 records May 18, 2026 passage and imposes a new 180-day data-center application/permit pause while its recital describes extending Ordinance 2025-28. It permits early rescission or extension; immediate effect is conditional on the required Council votes. Identity/continuity between the acts, actual effectiveness, operative interval, later action and the legacy replacement classification remain unresolved. [VERIFY: instrument relationship, operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
current_status.reason: Signed Ordinance 2026-06 contradicts the prior statement that no extension or replacement moratorium was found.
